title: Reproduce and improve context-transfer time decoding in mouse medial entorhinal cortex
scientific_question: Does shaping experience change how MEC activity represents elapsed trial time across odor-sequence contexts, and can a fixed decoder-building policy improve held-trial cross-context decoding under equal calibration access?

actor_semantics.attempts: Paper_data and paper_data_code are conditions of one paper family; eight outer cases/ten folds/three contexts are not additional benchmark registrations.
actor_semantics.improvement: Fixed submitted prediction program, not live query-by-query code changes. A later investigative arm would require separately reviewed equal-information protocol; it is not silently added here.
actor_semantics.reproduction: Tool-using analysis and Python program production allowed within isolated task. Outcomes are numeric reconstruction plus provenance, not tool-call count.

conditions.exposure: Full final paper and necessary processed source data; no official implementation, owner reference code, cached predictions, published source tables with per-query answers or private scorer inputs. Candidate writes its own analysis.

Same final paper and same processed data plus an explicitly listed, rights-cleared official source-code snapshot. Code view preserves executable analysis and declared dependencies; answer caches/data are excluded transparently and identically as data, not silently edited out of code. Current source snapshot has a licensing/admission gate.

owner_source_target.caveat: Published figure statistics treat sessions as units; reproduction reports this faithfully and separately reports mouse-grouped summaries. It must not represent the published session-level test as independent-animal inference.
owner_source_target.context_pairs: 3 within and 6 across from LS,SL,SS; all-context decoder is not part of Figure6f score
owner_source_target.session_weights: equal context-pair weighting after averaging rows within each test context; then original absolute gap per session
owner_source_target.source_statistic: scipy.stats.ttest_ind(SL_only session gaps,standard session gaps), default equal_var=True

improvement.aggregation: average bins within each trial, trials within each ordered source/test-context pair, six cross-context pairs within session, sessions within mouse, then equal eight-mouse mean. Report both four-mouse shaping strata and all three within-context pairs separately.
baseline_portfolio: fresh official source LDA on identical split/inputs
regularized LDA with development-only hyperparameter selection (solver lsqr; shrinkage auto or0.01,0.1,0.5), original SVD LDA retained as anchor
constant-bin prior selected only on calibration; no-neural shape/order surrogate controls
improvement.context_access: For each source-context decoder, fit on that context only; evaluate LS,SL,SS equally. No query context, trial outcome, group, clock, row order or target bin supplied. Candidate cannot substitute an all-context decoder for a cross-context source-restricted comparison.
improvement.endpoint: mouse-macro cross-context circular squared error in seconds squared; lower is better
improvement.evaluation_split: Eight outer leave-one-mouse-out cases. Each fresh actor sees only seven development mice. Before held-mouse calibration is released, freeze algorithm source, hyperparameters/selection policy and artifact hashes. Fixed policy may fit session-specific decoder parameters on calibration trials of the held mouse; it cannot change policy after seeing that mouse.
improvement.inference: Report all eight paired mouse-level loss differences. The 256-sign enumeration is a descriptive symmetry diagnostic (tail fraction), not a calibrated p-value: leave-one-mouse-out development sets overlap, so the resulting loss differences are not established independent. A calibrated inferential claim requires a separately justified joint sign-exchangeability design. No significance/SOTA claim from this enumeration; no seed/cell/trial pseudoreplication.
improvement.novelty_limit: All source recordings and paper are public. Local answer isolation is not proof of absence from model pretraining. Paper-wide and code-cache contamination audit required; reproduction and improvement actors/history must be separate.
improvement.prediction_geometry: Row-wise offline decoding, matching the selected ephys LDA observation unit. One output is a function of its fixed fitted artifact and one neural feature vector; cross-query recurrent state, complete ordered trial geometry, query batch position/size and evaluation step counters are not inputs. Query row order/batch partition changes must preserve predictions after opaque-ID alignment. This pointwise contract is an explicit extension restriction, not a claim to reproduce an RNN sequence task.
improvement.state_isolation: Fresh restricted process and writable storage for EVERY outer-mouse/session/query-fold/source-context fit+predict unit. That unit receives only the fixed immutable policy/development assets, its source-context calibration, then its query vectors and its own fitted artifact. No other-fold or other-context calibration, fitted artifacts, query outputs or mutable state is accessible. Owner aggregates after all isolated units close. Ten-fold calibration/query reuse across different units cannot become a cache channel. Isolation enforcement is a constructor/runtime admission gate. Fresh isolation never resets the original outer-case absolute deadline or aggregate CPU/memory/PID/output budget; all units share the same remaining allowance and complete cleanup accounting.
improvement.transfer_claim: Unseen-animal algorithm/policy transfer with within-session calibration; not zero-shot shared-unit decoding across mice.
improvement.within_session_split: All trials and all cells/time bins of a trial stay together. Ten folds use authenticated source trial ordering and np.array_split semantics; each query fold is disjoint from its nine-fold calibration. Empty folds or absent required context/class support fail admission, not silent dropping.

inactive_instruction_text.reproduction:
# Reproduce the paper's MEC context-transfer result

Given the final paper and the admitted processed MEC recordings, reconstruct the quantitative result shown in Figure 6f: how trial-time decoding changes between within-context and across-context evaluation for the two shaping histories.

Use all admitted animals and recording sessions. Derive the result from the processed spike-event data. Provide a runnable analysis program, the per-session context-pair error table with units, within/across summaries, the plotted comparison and its statistical calculation, and a concise account of your choices and limitations. State the experimental unit used in each calculation; distinguish repeated sessions from independent mice. Explain any ambiguity between the paper and the materials available in your condition, rather than silently changing the cohort or interpreting a published statistic as a new result.

Your packet states whether official analysis source is available. The paper-only condition includes no reference implementation. Both conditions have the same paper and source recording data; cached author predictions and final answer tables are not analysis inputs. Numerical agreement, method validity and provenance are reported separately. An exact-source match by itself is not a comprehensive score for scientific reasoning.

Do not access the network or owner reference outputs. Every run must stay within the supplied runtime, input manifest and attempt budget. Report a missing or contradictory required input instead of substituting a smaller dataset.

This prompt is inactive until the constructor, reference comparison and paper-method ambiguity gates in the owner contract have been resolved.
inactive_instruction_text.improvement:
# Improve held-trial cross-context time decoding

Develop a fixed program that builds a decoder of elapsed trial time from MEC feature vectors. You receive development mice and a source-context calibration interface. An outer evaluation uses a mouse absent from development. Your code and hyperparameter-selection policy are frozen before that mouse's calibration data are released. The policy may then fit session-specific parameters from the allowed calibration trials.

For each fit, use only the supplied source context. The evaluator scores that decoder on all three trial contexts, with the six cross-context pairs as the primary endpoint. Query IDs are opaque and unordered; submit one integer time-bin prediction in 0..39 for every supplied ID. Bins are spaced0.5seconds on a20second circular interval. The loss is squared shortest circular time distance in seconds squared. All forty bins in every query trial are evaluated. Scores average bins within trials, trials within each context pair, context pairs within sessions, sessions within each mouse and then mice equally. Within-context results and both shaping strata are also reported.

Compare against the fixed reference baselines on exactly the same cases and calibration access. Improvement is the paired per-mouse decrease in cross-context loss, not an increase in the between-minus-within gap. The released results will include every mouse. Leave-one-mouse-out development sets overlap, so eight mice do not automatically produce eight independent loss differences; any sign-enumeration summary is descriptive, not a calibrated significance test. A better score is not by itself a broad SOTA or causal claim.

Every session/query-fold/source-context fit and its prediction phase runs in fresh restricted process/storage with only its own calibration and fitted artifact. No state, calibration, artifact, prediction or feedback from any other fold/context is available. This matters because a query trial in one fold is calibration in other folds.

No query timestamps, temporal ordering, trial outcomes, row-to-time mapping, private labels or score feedback are available. Do not modify code after held calibration is released, fit to query data, load cached author answers, or change the admitted cohort. The task is offline feature-vector decoding with declared preprocessing, not causal streaming inference. All code/source/data access is restricted to the manifest for your condition.

The held-mouse evaluation represents algorithm transfer with within-session calibration. It does not assume neuron identities align across mice. This is a prospective extension of the paper; its numeric improvement endpoint was not a published paper result.

This prompt is inactive until the complete source roster, trial support, rights, runtime, reference baselines and leakage controls pass admission.

The prediction interface is pointwise: a fixed fitted artifact and the current neural vector determine its output. Do not use query position, batch boundaries, a recurrent step counter or state carried from other query rows. The owner mixes rows across trials/contexts and will require identical ID-aligned outputs under different row orders and batch partitions. Neural-unit columns retain the same order as calibration. Offline within-trial feature construction is performed before this mixing. This is a declared row-wise ephys decoding extension, not a shuffled version of the paper's RNN sequence task.
